title: Insert interval
statement: Insert a new interval into a sorted list of disjoint closed intervals, merging where needed; return the sorted disjoint result.
hints: Three phases: intervals entirely before, the ones overlapping (absorb them), intervals entirely after.

solution.explanation: The input is already sorted, so don't sort: walk once in three phases. Copy intervals ending before the new start; absorb every interval that overlaps, widening [s, e]; copy the rest. Recognising that sorted input deserves an O(n) answer, not a re-sort, is the point.
solution.python:
def insert(intervals, new):
    s, e = new
    out = []
    i, n = 0, len(intervals)
    while i < n and intervals[i][1] < s:
        out.append(intervals[i]); i += 1
    while i < n and intervals[i][0] <= e:
        s = min(s, intervals[i][0]); e = max(e, intervals[i][1]); i += 1
    out.append([s, e])
    out.extend(intervals[i:])
    return out
